memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: “She will give birth to a son, and you are to give Him the name Jesus, because He will save His people from their sins.” -Matthew 1:21

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
Christmas can never truly exist without Christ. The moment Christ is pushed aside, Christmas slowly turns into a hollow celebration. Lights sparkle, songs play sweetly, gifts are exchanged, but the darkness of the heart remains unchanged. People admire the manger, yet reject the Lord who lay in it. Celebration without surrender does not produce transformation; it produces deception.

The true meaning of Christmas is not found in outward decorations, but in inward submission to God’s rule. Jesus did not come to this world merely to be celebrated, but to save our souls. The Child born in the manger willingly walked toward the Cross. Christmas without repentance may give temporary happiness, but never lasting peace. Christ did not come to decorate our lives; He came to rescue them from destruction.

When Christmas places Christ back at the center, revival begins. Programs turn into worship, traditions become holy, and noise is transformed into surrender. The real question is not whether we celebrate Christmas, but whether Christ is truly Lord over it. A Christ-filled Christmas restores hearts; a Christless Christmas becomes nothing more than an empty event.
What kind of Christmas are we celebrating?

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: “If Christ is not Lord of all, He is not Lord at all.” - A. W. Tozer

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, Forgive us for forgetting Your lordship in the midst of celebrating Your birth. Help us to place You back at the center of our hearts in this season. Grant us not only joy, but true repentance.
Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: A Christless Christmas is only tradition without transformation. Today, make room in your heart and enthrone Jesus as King.
